text:
alex: quick heads-up — the canary that flipped the new attention kernel + tighter KV-cache stride on mixtral-8x is showing a weird signal: overall tokens/sec up, but eval failure rate jumped from 0.9% -> 4.6% and p95 latency +18ms.

riya: saw the alert. which kernel variant? was it the fused-attn-8bit change?

alex: yes, fused-attn-avx2 -> fused-attn-optimized (small-window) + kv_stride from 1 -> 2. rollout was canary 10% traffic. infra-bot reported deploy id deploy-20260309-77.

sam: grabbing profiler traces now. initial look: CPU side shows more work in the kv-restitch path during decode. GPU timeline shows shorter matmul but more frequent small-kernel launches. could be increased kernel launch overhead for short sequences.

sam: profiling snippet:
```
# timeline slices (canary vs control)
canary: 12ms kernel-launch overhead per token chunk, 6 small kernels
control: 4ms kernel-launch overhead, 2 kernels
```

matt: is the eval regression quality-related (answers wrong) or timeout/errors?

alex: mostly eval suite failures flagged by fuzzy match thresholds (answers truncated/incomplete), not timeouts. some completions have garbled tokens at boundaries.

riya: that smells like RoPE or KV-index mismatch — changing kv_stride can shift alignment of cached kv chunks. Did we also change RoPE scaling or head dim packing for this build?

alex: we only changed kernel selection and kv_stride for batching heuristics. but the optimized kernel has a slightly different chunking strategy (it pads/rounds heads differently). logs show warnings about rounding when head_dim%16 !=0.

sam: attaching eval case example:
```
--- input id: eval-20260308-119
expected: "...the capital is Paris"
actual:   "...the capital is Par"
log: kv-cache-chunk 3 misaligned, decode stopped early
```

riya: ok that's consistent with kv cache alignment causing partial truncation at boundaries. quantization toggles could make it noisier but we didn't flip quant there, right?

alex: correct, quantization unchanged. only kernel + kv_stride.

matt: given impact, recommend immediate rollback on canary and open a follow-up: revert kernel swap for mixtral-8x until we fix alignment or make kernel compatibility checks. canary is at 10% so we can abort cleanly.

infra-bot: rollback initiated: deploy-rollback deploy-20260309-77 -> deploy-20260309-76 by matt at 2026-03-09T15:12:30Z :warning:

sam: agreed. also creating perf/profile tickets: one to add runtime validation that compares kv-chunking behavior between kernels (unit tests + small decode diff), one to add eval smoke on canary (run small prompt set before routing live).

riya: action items I can take: 1) reproduce locally with small seq batch and reproduce misaligned KV chunk. 2) add assertion in runtime that checks kv-index monotonicity across chunks. 3) test head_dim padding in optimized kernel with non-16-aligned dims.

alex: thanks — also let's not forget to check Mixtral vs Qwen parity: Qwen uses different head packing so this kernel might not misbehave there but we should test.

matt: I'll hold canary off until we have the kv alignment test and a quick smoke-run. Sam, grab traces and put into the perf bucket.

sam: done. uploaded traces -> s3://redwood-perf/mixtral/2026-03-09/canary-77.tar.gz. PR for rollback is up: https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/4981 :arrow_up_small:

alex: planning note — if we want optimized kernel benefits we should: a) make kernel advertise compatibility set (head dims, packing, kv_stride semantics), b) add automated binary-level checks during rollout, c) run small eval suite at 1% traffic before widening.

riya: +1. also add a short integration test that diff-decodes a few golden prompts comparing both kernels and fails the canary if mismatch > threshold.

matt: good plan. reassigning to eng-runtime:perf. tagging @sam @riya for follow-ups.

infra-bot: deploy-rollback completed successfully at 2026-03-09T15:14:02Z. canary traffic reverted.

alex: thanks all. next steps: small patch for kv-index assertion, unit test for misalignment, and a canary-smoke job that runs eval-set-quick. I'll file the design doc for kernel compatibility checks later today. :thumbsup:
